AI_IMPL_PROMPT

Goal

Create a production-quality public OLCR product website that demonstrates OLCR itself and also serves as a real benchmark for:

1. Anime.js MCP integration
2. Anime.js v4 implementation quality
3. shadcn MCP usage
4. Playwright MCP browser verification
5. OLCR Coding Orchestrator frontend implementation quality
6. later OLCR FIX-mode repair quality

The site should feel like a premium modern developer product website with cinematic scroll-driven storytelling.

Use the interaction philosophy of high-end Apple product pages as inspiration:

- large typography
- strong visual hierarchy
- generous whitespace
- sticky/pinned visual sequences
- content that changes progressively while scrolling
- restrained but polished motion
- sections that feel like a continuous narrative
- product concepts visually explained rather than only listed

Do NOT reproduce Apple's actual:

- layout
- graphics
- copy
- assets
- product page structure
- branding

Create an original OLCR design.


Product

Name:

OLCR

Type:

Local-first AI development / orchestration tool

Primary audience:

- developers
- local AI users
- AI-assisted software builders
- users interested in private/local coding workflows

Primary site goal:

Explain what OLCR is, why it exists, how it works, what integrations it contains, and direct users to GitHub.

Secondary goal:

Create a frontend implementation complex enough to meaningfully exercise Anime.js and later FIX mode.


Repository / Target Check

Before implementation, inspect the currently selected target repository/workspace.

Determine:

TARGET_REPO=
EXISTING_WEBSITE=
EXISTING_FRAMEWORK=
PACKAGE_MANAGER=
EXISTING_DESIGN_SYSTEM=
EXISTING_ANIMEJS_VERSION=
EXISTING_TAILWIND=
EXISTING_SHADCN=
BUILD_COMMAND=
DEV_COMMAND=
TEST_COMMAND=

If an existing website project already exists:

extend it while preserving its conventions where reasonable.

If this is a greenfield website workspace:

use the stack defined below.

Do not modify the OLCR application repository itself unless it is explicitly the selected target for the website.

Do not invent repository paths.


Required Technology Stack

For greenfield implementation use:

- Vite
- React
- TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS
- shadcn/ui
- Anime.js v4

Browser verification:

- Playwright MCP

Reference/tooling:

- Anime.js MCP
- shadcn MCP

Do NOT introduce:

- Next.js
- GSAP
- Framer Motion / Motion
- Three.js
- backend server
- database
- authentication
- CMS
- analytics
- Docker

unless the existing target repository already requires them.

Anime.js should be the primary JavaScript animation system for this benchmark.


Required MCPs

Persist equivalent:

required_mcps:
- animejs
- shadcn
- playwright

Real MCP evidence is required.

Do not consider the task fully verified based only on model prose.

Required evidence:

ANIMEJS_MCP_USED=YES
SHADCN_MCP_USED=YES
PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_USED=YES

Anime.js MCP usage must include at least one real Anime.js v4 reference/pattern lookup.

shadcn MCP usage must include a real registry/component lookup.

Playwright MCP usage must include real browser interaction/inspection.

If a required MCP cannot execute:

do not falsely claim VERIFIED completion.


Anime.js Version Rules

Use Anime.js v4.

Before implementation:

inspect target project's installed/declared Anime.js version.

If:

v4
→ continue

v3
→ stop normal v4 implementation and report CONFLICT_V3_V4 unless explicit migration is authorized

none
→ add Anime.js v4 as a project-local dependency according to existing dependency policy

unknown
→ do not guess compatibility

Do not mix Anime.js v3 and v4 APIs.


Brand Direction

This website is specifically for OLCR.

Use:

Background:
#000000 / near-black

Primary text:
#FFFFFF

OLCR accent:
#95E329

Supporting neutrals:
dark charcoal / gray / off-white

The OLCR green accent belongs to this OLCR site only.

Do not treat it as a reusable global frontend default for unrelated projects.


Visual Direction

Design character:

- premium
- technical
- minimal
- cinematic
- local-AI / developer-tool feel
- high contrast
- restrained green accent
- spacious
- intentionally composed
- not generic SaaS template

Avoid:

- every section being a rectangular card grid
- excessive glowing borders
- excessive gradients
- random glassmorphism
- giant amounts of decorative pills
- duplicated CTA blocks
- same GitHub button repeated in every section
- over-animation
- generic AI-generated landing-page appearance

Use fewer, stronger visual ideas.


Page Structure

The page must follow this narrative order:

SECTION-01
Hero / OLCR title

↓

OLCR philosophy

↓

SECTION-03
How OLCR works

↓

SECTION-04

↓

↓

Footer


SCREEN-01 / ROUTE

Route:

/

Single long-form scrolling homepage.

No multi-page routing required for MVP.


SECTION-01 — Hero

Purpose:

Immediately establish OLCR as the product.

Required content:

Very large:

OLCR

The title should dominate the initial viewport.

Include a concise supporting statement explaining the product without excessive copy.

Possible semantic direction:

"Local AI. Structured execution."

Exact final marketing copy may be refined, but do not make unsupported product claims.


Visual behavior:

Initial state should feel intentionally minimal.

As the user scrolls:

- OLCR typography changes position/scale subtly
- supporting content enters progressively
- visual depth develops
- transition naturally into the philosophy section

Use Anime.js.

Avoid a simple one-time fade-in as the entire hero animation.


SECTION-02 — OLCR Philosophy

Purpose:

Explain the principles behind OLCR.

The section should communicate ideas equivalent to:

- local-first execution
- user control
- structured AI work
- evidence over unsupported success claims
- planning before broad implementation
- tools used only when relevant
- bounded and observable execution

Do not invent guarantees not supported by the repository/product.

Presentation:

Do not use six identical cards.

Prefer a scroll narrative.

Example interaction pattern:

one large statement remains sticky
while supporting concepts progressively enter/change around it.

The scrolling experience should feel like concepts are being revealed, not like reading a static feature grid.


SECTION-03 — How OLCR Works

Purpose:

Provide a substantially more detailed explanation than a normal marketing site.

This is one of the main sections.

Explain the actual OLCR workflow based on repository evidence.

Inspect the OLCR project before writing factual architecture copy.

Possible conceptual stages may include, only when confirmed:

User request
→ conversation/project context
→ classification
→ planning
→ Coding Orchestrator
→ task execution
→ MCP/tool use
→ verification
→ final evidence/report

Do not hardcode this exact flow if repository evidence differs.

Visual treatment:

Create a large interactive/animated system visualization.

Recommended structure:

sticky left/right visual system
+
scrolling explanatory steps

or:

central pipeline
+
progressively activated nodes

As the user scrolls:

- current stage becomes prominent
- previous stage recedes
- relationships/lines animate
- descriptive copy changes
- system state visually advances

Use Anime.js for meaningful timeline/state transitions.

This section must not degrade into only static text cards.


SECTION-04 — OLCR APIs

Purpose:

Show APIs/integrations actually present in OLCR.

IMPORTANT:

Inspect the repository and derive the API list from authoritative implementation/configuration.

Do not fabricate integrations.

Previously known OLCR integrations may include things such as:

- EONET
- Federal Register
- PubChem
- OSRM
- SymPy-related local computation

but the current repository is authoritative.

Only publish integrations actually supported by current source.

Distinguish:

external APIs
from
local computation/providers

if appropriate.

Presentation:

Use visually varied integration rows/tiles.

Do not use the exact same card design as every previous section.

Animation:

As entries enter viewport:

- subtle stagger
- metadata reveals
- connecting line / indicator motion where useful

Animation must remain secondary to readability.


SECTION-05 — MCP Ecosystem

Purpose:

Explain MCP capabilities integrated into OLCR.

Inspect repository MCP manifests/configuration.

Only show currently known integrations and truthful status.

Possible integrations may include:

- Serena
- shadcn
- Playwright
- Anime.js
- DevDocs

but current repository state is authoritative.

Important:

If DevDocs is still disabled/security-blocked:

do NOT present it as an active production capability.

Represent status truthfully or omit it.

For each relevant MCP explain briefly:

name
role
when OLCR uses it

Examples of semantic roles:

Serena
→ complex repository/symbol analysis

shadcn
→ UI/component reference

Anime.js
→ animation/reference guidance

Playwright
→ browser verification

Do not claim actual behavior unless confirmed by repository evidence.


Animation treatment:

This section may use an orbital/network/toolchain visual metaphor, but keep it technically readable.

As user scrolls:

- one MCP becomes active
- its relationship to Coding Orchestrator is highlighted
- supporting description changes

Use Anime.js for transitions.


SECTION-06 — GitHub / Download

Purpose:

One decisive final CTA area.

Required:

GitHub button linking to:

https://github.com/nagix123-e/olcr

Future download button.

The download button is FRONTEND ONLY.

It must not:

- download a fake binary
- call a backend
- create an API
- install anything

Use a disabled or clearly unavailable state with wording equivalent to:

"Download — Coming Soon"

or a similarly polished label.

Do not mislead users into thinking a release file is currently available.


CTA hierarchy:

Primary:
GitHub

Secondary:
future Download

Do not repeatedly show the same GitHub + Download pair throughout adjacent sections.


Footer

Minimal.

Include:

OLCR
GitHub
appropriate lightweight copyright/project text

Do not create an oversized second CTA.


Animation Architecture

The goal is a scroll-driven experience, not random entrance animations.

Create an intentional motion system.

Use at least these categories where appropriate:

1. Hero transformation

2. Sticky scroll storytelling

3. Section progress transitions

4. Staggered text/data reveal

5. Architecture diagram state transitions

6. MCP/API reveal

7. Final CTA transition


Anime.js MCP

Before writing animation code:

query the Anime.js MCP for current v4 guidance relevant to:

- scroll-linked or scroll-triggered interaction
- timelines
- stagger
- React lifecycle/scoping
- reduced motion

Use real returned evidence.

Do not invent v4 API signatures.


React / Anime.js Lifecycle

Animations must respect React lifecycle.

Avoid:

- duplicate animations after rerenders
- orphaned listeners
- animation instances surviving unmount incorrectly
- uncontrolled global DOM selectors

Prefer component-local refs/scoping.

Exact implementation must follow current Anime.js v4 guidance from the MCP.


Scroll Implementation

Prefer native browser primitives plus Anime.js.

Possible supporting primitives:

- IntersectionObserver
- ResizeObserver
- requestAnimationFrame where justified
- CSS position: sticky
- CSS transforms

Do not add a second large animation framework.


Accessibility

Required:

prefers-reduced-motion support

If:

prefers-reduced-motion: reduce

then:

- disable or heavily simplify nonessential movement
- all content remains visible/readable
- navigation remains usable
- information must not depend on animation
- sticky sequences must not trap interaction

Semantic HTML required.

Visible keyboard focus required.

Buttons/links must have accessible names.

Decorative visual elements should not pollute the accessibility tree.


Responsive Design

Desktop is the richest cinematic experience.

Required widths to verify approximately:

1440px
1280px
768px
390px

Mobile must not simply shrink the desktop sticky animation.

For narrow displays:

- simplify animation
- remove unnecessary pinned sequences
- preserve narrative ordering
- maintain readable typography
- prevent horizontal overflow

The giant OLCR hero title must remain intentional on mobile without clipping important content.


Performance

Favor:

transform
opacity

for high-frequency animation.

Avoid unnecessary layout thrashing.

Do not animate large numbers of elements continuously without reason.

Avoid an always-running animation loop when the section is offscreen.

Respect reduced motion.

Do not add huge decorative assets just to imitate premium visuals.


shadcn Usage

Actually consult shadcn MCP.

Use shadcn only where it improves implementation.

Possible components:

Button
Badge
Separator
Tooltip

Do not convert the entire visual site into default shadcn cards.

The site must still have a distinct OLCR identity.


Content Accuracy

Before writing architecture/API/MCP copy:

inspect OLCR repository evidence.

Distinguish:

CONFIRMED
from
ASSUMED

Do not publish assumptions as facts.

Do not expose:

secrets
local absolute paths
internal credentials
private system details

Do not expose unnecessary implementation internals on the public page.


UI Copy

Keep primary UI copy concise.

Avoid excessive buzzwords.

Prefer concrete statements about what OLCR actually does.

Do not claim:

"best"
"perfect"
"fully autonomous"
"guaranteed"
"enterprise-grade"

unless independently supported, which is not expected here.


Implementation Blueprint

Because this is a substantial frontend benchmark, create a short internal implementation blueprint before mutation.

Include:

- section/component structure
- animation ownership
- responsive strategy
- Anime.js lifecycle strategy
- MCP use
- browser verification strategy

Do not turn repo inspection into a user-visible implementation phase.


Suggested Component Shape

Exact paths/names must follow the actual repository, but conceptually separate:

App / Page shell

Hero
Philosophy
HowItWorks
APIIntegrations
MCPIntegrations
FinalCTA
Footer

plus reusable animation primitives/helpers only when they reduce duplication.

Do not create abstraction layers speculatively.


State

This site should need minimal application state.

Do not add global state management.

Prefer local component state and browser observation state.

No Redux/Zustand unless an existing target project already requires it.


Data

API and MCP display information should preferably come from local typed constants/data objects.

Example conceptual shape:

IntegrationItem {
    id
    name
    category
    description
    status?
}

Do not add a database or runtime API for static marketing content.


MVP Exclusions

Do NOT implement:

backend
authentication

release installer

unless separately requested later.


Implementation Order

Phase 1:

Inspect target project and OLCR repository evidence.

Resolve:

- target frontend stack
- current API list
- current MCP list/status
- Anime.js compatibility

Perform required MCP preflight/query.

Then implement the complete homepage.


Phase 2:

Run browser verification and correct implementation defects discovered by verification.

Do not perform unrelated visual redesign during verification.


Keep total phase count small.

Do not create separate phases for:

Repo inspection
planning
final report


Playwright Verification

Use real Playwright MCP.

Verify at minimum:

PAGE_LOAD=PASS

NO_HORIZONTAL_OVERFLOW_DESKTOP=PASS

NO_HORIZONTAL_OVERFLOW_MOBILE=PASS

GITHUB_LINK_PRESENT=PASS

GITHUB_LINK_TARGET_CORRECT=PASS

DOWNLOAD_BUTTON_PRESENT=PASS

DOWNLOAD_BUTTON_FRONTEND_ONLY=PASS

HERO_VISIBLE=PASS

PHILOSOPHY_SECTION_VISIBLE=PASS

HOW_IT_WORKS_SECTION_VISIBLE=PASS

API_SECTION_VISIBLE=PASS

MCP_SECTION_VISIBLE=PASS

FINAL_CTA_VISIBLE=PASS

ANIMEJS_EFFECT_OBSERVED=PASS

SCROLL_STATE_TRANSITION=PASS

MOBILE_LAYOUT=PASS

PREFERS_REDUCED_MOTION=PASS

CONSOLE_ERRORS=NONE_FROM_IMPLEMENTATION


Visual Review

Before declaring completion, inspect the rendered page.

Check:

- duplicated GitHub/download CTAs
- repeated identical card grids
- generic template appearance
- accidental huge blank regions
- weak content hierarchy
- unreadable small text
- hero clipping
- sticky-section overlap
- section transition discontinuity
- animation that obscures content
- animation too fast to understand
- excessive motion
- broken mobile composition
- inconsistent content widths


Do not use a subjective numeric design score.

Use concrete observed issues.


FIX Benchmark Preparation

This initial task is IMPLEMENTATION, not FIX.

Do not deliberately introduce bugs.

However, structure code so later observed defects can be repaired independently and verified.

After initial implementation:

report concrete remaining visual/runtime defects separately.

Do NOT perform speculative broad refactoring merely to make future FIX tests easier.

Later user requests such as:

"スクロールすると仕組みのセクションが一瞬消えるので直して"

or:

"スマホでOLCRのタイトルが右にはみ出すので修正して"

must be suitable for separate FIX-mode tasks.


Security / Safety

No secrets.

No destructive operations.

No modification outside selected website project except read-only inspection of OLCR source required to determine accurate product facts.

No commit.

No push.

No publish.

No deploy.


Done

The homepage is complete when:

- all six required narrative sections exist
- content is based on current OLCR evidence
- Anime.js v4 is genuinely used
- Anime.js MCP real tool evidence exists
- shadcn MCP real tool evidence exists
- Playwright MCP real verification exists
- scrolling produces meaningful progressive motion
- reduced-motion mode works
- desktop and mobile are usable
- GitHub CTA is correct
- future Download control is frontend-only and non-deceptive
- build succeeds
- implementation-origin console errors are absent
- no unsupported OLCR feature claims are present


FailureHandling

If Anime.js MCP is unavailable:

because it is explicitly required for this benchmark,
do not claim verified completion.

Report:

ANIMEJS_MCP=BLOCKED


If Anime.js project version is incompatible:

do not silently upgrade or mix API versions.

Report exact conflict.


If shadcn MCP fails:

because it is explicitly required for this benchmark,
do not falsely mark the benchmark fully verified.


If Playwright MCP cannot run:

implementation may exist,
but browser verification must remain:

NOT_RUN
or
BLOCKED

Never report PASS without execution.


If OLCR API/MCP facts cannot be confirmed:

omit uncertain claims or mark them unresolved.

Do not invent them.


Report

TARGET_REPO=
STACK=

ANIMEJS_PROJECT_VERSION=
ANIMEJS_VERSION_COMPATIBILITY=

ANIMEJS_MCP_REQUIRED=YES
ANIMEJS_MCP_USED=

SHADCN_MCP_REQUIRED=YES
SHADCN_MCP_USED=

PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_REQUIRED=YES
PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_USED=

OLCR_API_SOURCE=
OLCR_API_COUNT=

OLCR_MCP_SOURCE=
OLCR_MCP_COUNT=

IMPLEMENTED_SECTIONS=

ANIMATION_ARCHITECTURE=

REDUCED_MOTION=

DESKTOP_VERIFY=
MOBILE_VERIFY=

PLAYWRIGHT_VERIFY=

BUILD=
TESTS=
CONSOLE_ERRORS=

CHANGED_FILES=

UNVERIFIED=
UNRESOLVED=

OBSERVED_FIX_CANDIDATES=

NEXT=

COMMIT_CREATED=NO
PUSH=NO
PUBLISH=NOT_RUN
DEPLOY=NOT_RUN


Final Status

Use exactly one:

OLCR_ANIMATED_WEBSITE_VERIFIED

OLCR_ANIMATED_WEBSITE_PARTIAL

OLCR_ANIMATED_WEBSITE_BLOCKED
